content.text:
Spiked it rather than building it, which was the right call — it found a production bug and a licensing wall before any DataQ code changed.

## LocalStack is real, and blocked on you

The emulator exists and the approach is technically sound. But `localstack/snowflake:2026.6.0` **exits 55, "License activation failed"** with no auth token. There's no community tier — only a free non-commercial OSS licence by application. That's the same call you already made for Databricks Free Edition (gap G-h): fine for demo/eval, needs revisiting before anything commercial. Get a token at app.localstack.cloud and `./harness_local.sh snowflake localstack` runs the whole thing.

## So I split the spike, and settled the free half

The question divides into **our plumbing** (does DataQ survive a redirected host at all) and **their fidelity** (does LocalStack's SQL satisfy DataQ's queries). The first is emulator-independent, so I settled it against **fakesnow** (Apache-2.0, no account).

`local/snowflake_probe.py` runs DataQ's *real* functions — not equivalents, because a hand-rolled probe only proves the probe works. **6/6**: driver, DataQ's DSN through `connect_args`, volume + freshness monitors, the profiler aggregate, and the full GX `add_snowflake` → `run_expectations` chain with three expectations.

That pre-solves the part that would have cost you a day: the redirect **must** ride in SQLAlchemy `connect_args`. snowflake-sqlalchemy explicitly blocks `host` and `protocol` as URL query params — *"they change the connection target"* — and GX threads `kwargs['connect_args']` into its own `create_engine`. A query-string override is a dead end.

## The probe found a live bug on its first run

**[#1067](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1067)** — GX's `REQUIRED_QUERY_PARAMS` is `{"warehouse", "role"}`, but DataQ makes `role` optional for password auth and the connection test is deliberately GX-free. So a Snowflake connection created without a Role **tests green and fails every suite run**. Only the expectation half fails — monitors never touch GX — so it looks *partly* alive, which is worse. Filed P1, not fixed: it wants its own PR, and I'd want to check prod for role-less rows first, since the natural fix would newly reject them on edit.

## The rule I'd want on the record

**An emulator is continuity, not coverage.** A green suite against one is not evidence the Snowflake integration works — its `information_schema`, timestamp types and identifier folding are its own implementation. That's precisely what hid UC freshness returning a `str` (#953) and Parquet's Arrow dtypes (#520), and it's *worse* than a fixture because it looks like a live run. That warning is now in the probe, the compose file and the README, so a future reader can't take an emulator run as a live one.

## What's in the harness

Two opt-in profiles (`fakesnow`, `localstack`), neither starting by default; `./harness_local.sh snowflake [which]` starts and probes in one command. The **harness side needs no DataQ change** — `_harness.py` reads `SNOWFLAKE_HOST/PORT/PROTOCOL` and passes them only when set, so the cloud path is unchanged by construction. Two traps handled: LocalStack routes Snowflake by the `snowflake.` Host prefix, so it's published as a network alias rather than reached by service name; and `docker compose` interpolates **every** service regardless of profile, so my first `${VAR:?}` guard broke the plain `up` for the whole working stack — caught by testing the default path, not by reasoning about it.

Also: **PR #1065 has gone from `BLOCKED` to `CLEAN`**, 15 checks green. Still unmerged — your call.

Two decisions waiting: the LocalStack token, and whether DataQ gets the `host`/`port`/`protocol` field at all. My read is that the field's real justification isn't the wind-down — it's that [snowflake.py:11](backend/app/datasources/snowflake.py#L11) admits the Snowflake runner has **no end-to-end automated coverage**, and fakesnow in CI would give it some for the first time.

let's kill the localstack [ I don't want any more non OSS license resources even if it's just for harness]. Just keep a record what we evaluated so far somewhere. and merge the changes, and sync main.
Agreed — and that's a cleaner rule than the one I was applying. Removing it everywhere and recording why.

#### Evaluated and rejected: LocalStack for Snowflake (2026-07-27)

Recorded so the decision is not re-litigated, and because the *reason* generalises.

**What it is.** A Snowflake emulator from LocalStack, `localstack/snowflake`. On
paper the stronger option: it documents dynamic tables, streams, tasks and
stages/`COPY INTO`, so the dbt `ANALYTICS_STG` → `ANALYTICS` path — which fakesnow
almost certainly cannot carry — might have survived offline.

**Why it is out.** It is **not open source and has no community tier.** The image
exits **55, "License activation failed"**, with no auth token; a free licence
exists only by non-commercial application. That was enough on its own:

> **Nothing in this harness may require a commercial licence** — not even here,
> where the repo is untracked and undistributed. The DataQ rule (CONTRIBUTING
> rule 40 / ADR 0031) is about what DataQ *ships*; this is the stricter
> harness-side rule, adopted deliberately on 2026-07-27. A licence gate on a
> contingency stack defeats the contingency: the point of an offline harness is
> that it keeps running when accounts lapse, and a licence is one more account
> that can lapse. Trading an Azure subscription for a LocalStack one is not a
> wind-down.

It is also the same shape as the Databricks Free-Edition gap (**G-h**): fine for
demo/eval, needs re-deciding before anything commercial. One such open item is
enough.

**What was verified before rejecting** (so a re-evaluation starts here, not from
scratch): the image pulls and starts; it hard-fails without a token, so nothing
about its *fidelity* was ever observed — the "documents dynamic tables" claim
above is from its docs, **unverified**. Two integration details were established
and would still apply to any future attempt: it multiplexes AWS and Snowflake on
one port and routes by the `snowflake.` **Host-header prefix** (so inside a compose
network it must be reached via a network alias, never the service name), and
`docker compose` interpolates **every** service regardless of profile, so a
`${VAR:?}` guard on an opt-in service breaks the plain `up` for the whole stack.

**If the dbt/dynamic-table gap ever needs closing**, look for an Apache/MIT
alternative or point dbt at a local warehouse it can actually build in — do not
reopen this one.

---
name: feedback-no-commercial-licence-even-in-harness
description: Nothing in the DataQ harness may require a commercial licence — stricter than CONTRIBUTING rule 40, which only governs what DataQ ships
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Decided 2026-07-27, rejecting LocalStack for Snowflake: **no non-OSS-licensed
resource may be used anywhere in the project — including the untracked harness.**
Do not propose one, even scoped to local dev, even behind an opt-in profile, even
with a free non-commercial tier available by application.

**Why:** CONTRIBUTING rule 40 / ADR 0031 govern what DataQ *distributes*, so a
harness-only dependency technically passes them — that is the loophole this closes.
A licence gate on a *contingency* stack defeats the contingency: the whole point of
the offline harness is that it keeps running when accounts lapse, and a licence is
one more account that can lapse. Trading an Azure subscription for a vendor one is
not a wind-down. It also adds a second "free for now, re-decide before commercial"
open item alongside the Databricks Free-Edition gap (G-h).

**How to apply:** when picking harness tooling, check the licence *first* and pick
the Apache/MIT option even when the licensed one has more features. Worked example:
LocalStack for Snowflake documents dynamic tables/streams/tasks (fakesnow does not)
and would have kept the dbt ANALYTICS path alive offline — rejected anyway, and the
gap left open rather than paid for. Weak copyleft is fine with notices; AGPL is fine
*in the harness only* (MinIO) since it is undistributed, but never in DataQ's own
compose. See [[project_harness_env]] and [[feedback_working_agreements]].

Record every such evaluation rather than only the outcome: the harness README carries
what was verified before rejecting, so a re-evaluation starts from evidence instead of
from scratch.

- **MinIO is AGPL-3.0.** Fine here (this repo is untracked and DataQ does not
  distribute it) but it must never enter DataQ's own `docker-compose.yml` —
  CONTRIBUTING rule 40 / ADR 0031. SeaweedFS or s3proxy (Apache-2.0) are the
  compliant substitutes; DataQ's `endpoint_url` works with either.
- **Snowflake/Databricks are not Azure** and survive an Azure wind-down as long as
  those accounts live. Two routes to a *fully* offline warehouse, below.

### Snowflake stand-in (`./harness_local.sh snowflake`)

One opt-in compose profile — **fakesnow**, Apache-2.0, DuckDB-backed, no account
and no token. It does not start by default.

**`local/snowflake_probe.py` is the acceptance test for it.** It runs DataQ's
*real* functions — `build_connection_string`, `run_monitors_over_engine`,
`build_aggregate_query`, `run_expectations` — not hand-rolled equivalents, so a
PASS is about DataQ, not about the probe. fakesnow answers all six: driver,
DataQ's DSN through `connect_args`, volume + freshness monitors, the profiler
aggregate, and the full GX `add_snowflake` → `run_expectations` chain.

That settles the **DataQ-side plumbing** for any emulator: the redirect must ride
in SQLAlchemy `connect_args`, because snowflake-sqlalchemy blocks `host` and
`protocol` as URL query params ("they change the connection target"), and GX
threads `kwargs['connect_args']` into its own `create_engine`. DataQ would need a
`host`/`port`/`protocol` override on `SnowflakeConfig` at three engine sites. The
**harness side needs none** — `_harness.py` reads `SNOWFLAKE_HOST/PORT/PROTOCOL`
and passes them only when set, so the cloud path is unchanged by construction.

> **An emulator is CONTINUITY, not COVERAGE.** A green suite against one is not
> evidence DataQ's Snowflake integration works — its `information_schema`,
> timestamp types and identifier folding are its own implementation. That is the
> driver-boundary shape that hid the UC-freshness `str` bug (DataQ #953) and the
> Parquet Arrow-dtype bug (#520), and it is *worse* than a fixture because it
> looks like a live run. Label anything sourced from here as emulator-sourced.

The probe already earned its keep: it found **DataQ #1067** — a password-auth
Snowflake connection with no Role passes the connection test (which is GX-free)
and fails *every* suite run, because GX's `REQUIRED_QUERY_PARAMS` is
`{"warehouse", "role"}`.

- **Local Iceberg** is the other route and needs no third-party server at all:
  pointing the loads at `catalog_type=sql` + SQLite + a MinIO warehouse needs
  **no DataQ code** either — designed, not built.

#### Evaluated and rejected: LocalStack for Snowflake (2026-07-27)

Recorded so the decision is not re-litigated, and because the *reason* generalises.

═══════════ #1057 ═══════════
Merging #1056 breaks the GHCR eval stack until images are republished (compose-file/image version skew)

## The window

`docker-compose.ghcr.yml` and the published images are versioned **independently**:

- README / `docs/getting-started.md` tell evaluators to `curl` the compose file from **`main`**, so a merge is visible to users immediately.
- `.github/workflows/publish-images.yml` runs only on **`workflow_dispatch`** or a **`v*` tag push** — *not* on merge to `main`. `ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:latest` therefore does **not** move when a PR lands.

#1056 sets `SECRET_STORE: "openbao"` in that compose file. The currently-published `:latest` backend image validates `SECRET_STORE` against `Literal["env", "redis", "azure_key_vault"]`, so between merging #1056 and republishing images, the documented eval flow fails at startup with a pydantic error naming neither the cause nor a fix:

```
SECRET_STORE
  Input should be 'env', 'redis' or 'azure_key_vault'
```

That lands on exactly the artifact #1056 exists to make safer, and on the audience least equipped to debug it (a first-time evaluator with no source checkout).

## Fix

**Run `publish-images.yml` immediately after #1056 merges.** The new image accepts `openbao`, and compose + image are consistent again.

## Worth fixing properly

The skew is structural, not specific to this change: *any* PR touching `docker-compose.ghcr.yml` in a way that depends on new backend behaviour has the same window. Options:

1. Publish `:latest` on every merge to `main` (closes the window; costs a build per merge).
2. Have the eval compose pin a released tag rather than `:latest`, so the file and the image it names always match.
3. Keep it manual but add a PR-template checkbox: "touched `docker-compose.ghcr.yml`? → dispatch `publish-images` on merge".

(2) is the most honest — `:latest` floating against a `main`-tracked compose file is the actual defect — but it changes the "always get the newest" eval promise.

Found while verifying #1056; the `docker compose config` validation passes because the skew is a *runtime* mismatch, not a compose-syntax one.

═══════════ #1054 ═══════════
OpenBao/Vault: AppRole auth instead of a static token (ADR 0039 phase 2)

ADR [0039](docs/adr/0039-openbao-self-hosted-secret-backend.md) decision 4 ships phase-1 token auth: `OPENBAO_TOKEN` is a raw token sent as `X-Vault-Token`, held for the process lifetime and never renewed.

That is the right trade for the dev/eval stack (it replaces *no auth at all* — the plaintext `RedisSecretStore`), but it is not what a production self-hosted deployment should run:

- a static token does not expire on its own, so a leak is durable
- there is no renewal, so a TTL'd token silently starts 403ing mid-flight — the store logs `openbao_permission_denied` (ADR 0039 decision 6), but recovery is a restart
- the token has to be distributed to both the api and worker containers as plain env

**Wanted:** AppRole login (`role_id` + `secret_id` → `POST /v1/auth/approle/login` → renewable token), with:
- lazy login + cached token, re-login on 403
- periodic renewal before TTL expiry
- `OPENBAO_ROLE_ID` / `OPENBAO_SECRET_ID` settings alongside the existing `OPENBAO_TOKEN` (token stays for dev mode)

This is also the point at which `hvac` (Apache-2.0) is worth reconsidering — ADR 0039's "Alternatives considered" rejected it for three plain HTTP calls, but token lifecycle is exactly where a client library earns its keep.

Deferred from #1056 (the ADR 0039 implementation PR).

# that time; the structure, not the vigilance, is what needed fixing.
#
# So: if the compose comes from `main`, the image it names must come from `main`
# too. The `paths` filter keeps the cost off docs-only merges. Pinning a released
# tag in the compose file was the considered alternative and is rejected — it just
# inverts the skew, since a compose edit on `main` would then reference an image
# built before that edit.

        id: tags
        # Untrusted inputs come in via env (never interpolated into the script
        # body) so a dispatch `tag` value can't inject shell — IMAGE_NAME is the

          extra="${INPUT_TAG}"

          # Validate the extra tag against Docker's tag grammar (alphanumerics +
          # _.- , ≤128 chars, no leading separator) before it reaches the ref.
          if [ -n "$extra" ] && ! printf '%s' "$extra" | grep -Eq '^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,127}$'; then

            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -n "$extra" ]; then
            tags="${tags}"$'\n'"${image}:${extra}"
          fi
          echo "Publishing tags:"; echo "$tags"
          # Multi-line output for the build-push-action `tags:` list.
          {
            echo "tags<<EOF"
            echo "$tags"
            echo "EOF"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

# Path Filters and Tag Pushes in `push` Events

Based on the documentation provided, there is **no explicit guidance** on how `paths`/`paths-ignore` filters interact with `tags` filters when both are specified in a `push` event trigger.

The documentation states that path filters apply to branch pushes:

> "You can use the `paths` or `paths-ignore` filter to configure your workflow to run when a push to specific files occurs."

However, the documentation does not clarify whether path filters are evaluated for tag pushes or whether they suppress tag-triggered workflows.

**What we know:**
- Tag pushes are configured separately via the `tags` filter
- The documentation shows examples combining `branches` and `paths`, but provides no examples combining `tags` and `paths`
- There's a note about bulk operations: "Events will not be created for tags when more than three tags are pushed at once"

**Recommendation:** Test this behavior in your repository, or consult GitHub Support for definitive clarification on whether path filters apply to tag push events.

def _settings(**overrides: object) -> object:
    base: dict[str, object] = {
        "secret_store": "env",
        "azure_key_vault_url": None,
        "redis_url": "redis://localhost:6379/0",
        "openbao_addr": None,
        "openbao_token": None,

    }
    base.update(overrides)

def test_build_store_returns_env_store_by_default() -> None:
    store = _build_store(_settings())  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    assert isinstance(store, EnvSecretStore)


def test_build_store_returns_akv_store_when_configured() -> None:
    store = _build_store(
        _settings(
            secret_store="azure_key_vault",
            azure_key_vault_url="https://example.vault.azure.net/",
        )  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    )
    assert isinstance(store, AzureKeyVaultStore)


def test_build_store_raises_when_akv_url_missing() -> None:

        _build_store(_settings(secret_store="azure_key_vault"))  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def test_build_store_returns_openbao_store_when_configured() -> None:
    store = _build_store(

            openbao_addr="http://openbao:8200",
            openbao_token="tok",
        )  # type: ignore[arg-type]

def test_build_store_raises_when_openbao_addr_missing() -> None:

        _build_store(_settings(secret_store="openbao", openbao_token="tok"))  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def test_build_store_raises_when_openbao_token_missing() -> None:

        _build_store(
            _settings(secret_store="openbao", openbao_addr="http://openbao:8200")  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        )


def test_build_store_passes_configured_mount_through() -> None:
    """A non-default mount must reach the store — a prod vault rarely uses `secret/`,
    and silently reading from the wrong mount looks exactly like a missing secret."""
    store = _build_store(
        _settings(
            secret_store="openbao",
            openbao_addr="http://openbao:8200",
            openbao_token="tok",
            openbao_mount="dataq-kv",
        )  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    )
    assert isinstance(store, OpenBaoSecretStore)
    assert store._path("data", "x") == "/v1/dataq-kv/data/x"


def test_build_store_redis_mode_raises_with_migration_path() -> None:
    """ADR 0039 removed the plaintext store. The failure must NAME the replacement —

def _real_settings(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, **env: str) -> None:
    """Build Settings from env alone, ignoring any developer .env.app on disk.

def reset_secret_store_cache() -> None:
    """Test-only: clear the cached store so the next call rebuilds it.

    Closes the outgoing store's connection pool first (#1058). Test-only today, so
    each leaked pool was one idle connection — but the leak is in the *reset*, not
    in the tests, so it would become real the moment this is reused for config
    hot-reload, which is exactly the plausible next caller.

    `close()` is duck-typed rather than declared on the Protocol (see
    `OpenBaoSecretStore.close`), and is called OUTSIDE the lock: it does socket I/O,
    and the singleton is already detached, so a concurrent rebuild is both safe and
    independent of how long the close takes.
    """
    global _store_singleton
    with _store_lock:
        store, _store_singleton = _store_singleton, None
    close = getattr(store, "close", None)
    if callable(close):

    assert that `_build_store` still raises on an openbao config with no addr/token,

    the validator instead of the backstop, i.e. assert nothing about `_build_store`.

    Every test that CAN use a real `Settings` now does (`_settings_from_env`), so
    drift between `config.py`'s field names/Literal and what `_build_store` reads is
    caught where it is catchable.

    base: dict[str, object] = {
        "secret_store": "env",
        "azure_key_vault_url": None,
        "redis_url": "redis://localhost:6379/0",
        "openbao_addr": None,

    base.update(overrides)

# (this subscription caps Flexible Servers at 1, so the app shares the harness's
# server — renamed neutrally to dataq-pg-* / purpose=dataq-shared). The app connects
# as the least-privilege `dataq_app` role, which OWNS only the `dataq` database (no
# access to the `airflow` metadata DB on the same server).
#
# The `dataq_app` role + `dataq` database are provisioned out-of-band (a one-off
# psql against the server — see deploy/terraform/README.md "Shared Postgres"),
# keeping this stack connection-free (no postgres provider / no plan-time DB
# connection, so it stays CI-friendly). Its password is passed in as the sensitive
# var.app_db_password and injected as the DATABASE_URL Container App secret.
#
# Runtime reachability: the ACA apps connect over the server's allow-Azure-services
# firewall rule (the apps are Azure services), same as airflow.
#
# SECURITY CONSTRAINT — the single-role model is load-bearing, not just tidy.
# PostgreSQL's referential-integrity check switches to the REFERENCED TABLE'S OWNER
# before invoking an implicit cast on the FK value (ri_triggers.c). A role that can
# CREATE TYPE / FUNCTION / CAST and holds REFERENCES on another owner's table can
# therefore run its own SQL as that owner — reaching COPY ... TO PROGRAM if the owner
# has pg_execute_server_program. Unpatched upstream as of 2026-07-24.
# We are not exposed because there is exactly ONE app role (`dataq_app`) and it is
# not shared with any untrusted party. Adding a second, less-trusted role to the
# `dataq` database is what would create the exposure — so do not, without revisiting
# this. See the guardrail row in docs/progress.md.

data "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server" "shared" {
  name                = var.shared_pg_server_name
  resource_group_name = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
}

locals {
  # psycopg2 URL the backend Settings read as DATABASE_URL. sslmode=require —
  # Flexible Server enforces TLS. The password is URL-encoded so a future value
  # containing URL-significant chars (@ : / ? #) can't break DSN parsing (#395);
  # app_db_user/name are controlled alnum identifiers, no encoding needed.
  database_url = join("", [
    "postgresql+psycopg2://",
    var.app_db_user, ":", urlencode(var.app_db_password),
    "@", data.azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.shared.fqdn, ":5432/",
    var.app_db_name, "?sslmode=require",
  ])
}

Hardware security modules (HSMs) are tamper-resistant hardware devices that help secure cryptographic processes by generating, protecting, and managing keys used for encrypting data, decrypting data, creating digital signatures, and creating digital certificates. gh issue comment 435 --body 'Checked 2026-07-27. **The stated premise is stale, but the issue is still blocked — for a different and harder reason.** Not implementing; recording the findings so the AC can be corrected.

## The AC premise no longer holds

> _(build blocked while no cloud target)_

There has been a cloud target since 2026-06-28: `deploy/terraform/azure/` is applied and running. So that half of the blocker is gone.

## The real blocker: the database is not in our IaC, and CMK is creation-time-only

Two independent findings, either of which is sufficient:

**1. DataQ'"'"'s Terraform does not own the Postgres server.** [`postgres.tf`](deploy/terraform/azure/postgres.tf) declares it as a `data "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server" "shared"` — the subscription caps Flexible Servers at 1, so the app shares the harness'"'"'s server and only provisions a distinct `dataq` database + least-privilege role out-of-band. There is no `azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server` resource in this stack to assert encryption on, or to attach a key to.

**2. CMK cannot be enabled on an existing server, at all.** Microsoft is explicit ([data encryption at rest](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/postgresql/security/security-data-encryption)):

> You can select the mode only at server creation time. You can'"'"'t change the mode from one to another for the lifetime of the server.

The only route is [restoring a backup onto a new server](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/postgresql/security/security-configure-data-encryption#configure-data-encryption-with-customer-managed-key-on-existing-servers) and choosing CMK there. So CMK is not a Terraform toggle on what we run — it is **a new server plus a data migration**, and it collides with the 1-server subscription cap that produced the shared-server design in the first place.

## And a conflict with a decision already taken

Our Key Vault deliberately runs `key_vault_purge_protection = false` so a destroy/re-apply can reuse the vault name (recorded in [`deploy/README.md`](deploy/README.md), and re-affirmed at the W7 externals close as "left off — demo-scoped vault"). Per the same docs, if the vault holding the key is **deleted**, the server goes `Inaccessible` and denies all connections. A deliberately-destroyable vault is therefore the wrong place to hold a CMK; adopting CMK means reversing that decision (and purge protection is irreversible once enabled).

## What is actually true today, and what is cheap

**Encryption at rest is already satisfied, unconditionally:**

> Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server always encrypts all data at rest. This data includes all system and user databases, server logs, write-ahead log segments, and backups.

Service-managed keys are the default and require no action. The same is true of Key Vault, Log Analytics and App Insights — the other stateful resources this stack owns — where at-rest encryption is platform-default and not expressible as a Terraform assertion.

So the **documentation half of this issue is the whole cheap half, and it is the half that was actually asked for**: the original wording is "satisfied … but our Terraform neither asserts it nor offers CMK, **and it'"'"'s undocumented (no evidence for a customer security review)". Writing that evidence down costs little and discharges the GDPR Art 32 / HIPAA §164.312(a)(2)(iv) ask for a reviewer.

## Suggested AC rewrite

- [ ] Document the at-rest encryption posture per resource (what encrypts what, with which key, and the citation) — the customer-security-review artifact
- [ ] Record that CMK is **creation-time-only** and therefore out of scope for the current shared server; note the two prerequisites it would impose (a dedicated Flexible Server, and a purge-protected vault, reversing the recorded decision)
- [ ] Revisit only if a customer requires key custody, or when #505 (AWS/GCP IaC) creates a stack that owns its own database

Leaving open and in `v1.1 Week 7 — stretch`, retitled in effect from "assert + offer CMK" to "document the posture; CMK deferred with reasons".' 2>&1 | tail -2

Progress report, since this is a long run — two done and one assessed, two remaining.

**Merged already this turn:** #1065 (S3-compatible endpoints) and #1068 (post-merge bookkeeping). Main is synced and clean.

**PR [#1069](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1069) — open, CI green (14/14), `CLEAN`:**

**`Fixes #1057`** — GHCR images now publish on merge to `main`, not only on manual dispatch. Two things worth calling out. First, I verified the *immediate* breakage was already gone: the publish run built `908e608b`, the #1056 merge commit itself, 36 seconds after merge — so nothing is broken for evaluators right now, and only the structure needed fixing. Second, I nearly introduced a silent regression: combining `paths` with a `tags` filter *looks* like it would stop release publishes. It doesn't — path filters are ignored for tag pushes — but I checked rather than reasoned, and recorded it inline so nobody "fixes" it later. I rejected the issue's own preferred option (pin a released tag in the compose): it inverts the skew rather than removing it.

**`Fixes #1058`** — the pooled-client leak on cache reset, plus the two test-quality gaps. The ownership model matters more than the leak: `close()` only closes a client this store built, because closing an injected one would break both a caller reusing the pool and the MockTransport doubles the suite depends on. I kept `close()` off the `SecretStore` Protocol — 32 test doubles implement it structurally under the `backend/tests` mypy gate, so declaring it there buys one real `close()` for 32 no-op bodies. Both behaviours mutation-checked: reverting the close, and dropping the ownership check, each kill exactly one intended test.

One correction to the issue: it asked me to convert *all* `_build_store` tests to a real `Settings`. That's wrong for four of them — `Settings` now rejects exactly the states they assert (openbao without addr/token, and `redis`), so a real model can't reach them, and using one would silently test the validator instead of the backstop. Converted the rest; documented why the stand-in stays.

**[#435](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/435#issuecomment-5089879502) — checked, and the ticket's premise is stale but it's still blocked, for a harder reason.** "Blocked while no cloud target" hasn't been true since 2026-06-28. The real blockers: our Terraform **doesn't own the Postgres server** (it's a `data` source on the shared harness server, because the subscription caps Flexible Servers at 1), and Azure CMK is **creation-time-only** — *"You can select the mode only at server creation time"* — so it's a new server plus a data migration, not a Terraform toggle. It also collides with a decision you already took: our vault deliberately runs `purge_protection = false` so it can be destroyed and re-applied, and deleting the vault holding a CMK makes the database permanently `Inaccessible`. Encryption at rest is already unconditionally satisfied by service-managed keys; the *documentation* half is the cheap half and is the actual ask ("no evidence for a customer security review"). I posted a rewritten AC and left it open in W7 stretch.

**Still to do:** #1059 (orphaned secrets) and #1054 (AppRole) are each feature-sized — a store-seam addition plus a beat janitor, and a token-lifecycle implementation. Both touch `secrets.py`, which the review agent is currently reading, so I'm holding edits until it reports rather than reviewing a moving target.

On #1059 I'll flag one design intention now, because it's a judgement call you may want to overrule: the issue proposes a sweep that **purges** unreferenced credentials, and those are real warehouse credentials in production Key Vault. I plan to mirror `sweep_orphan_assets` (generous grace period from the vault's own `created_time`, prefix-scoped, `retention_days <= 0` as an off-switch) but default it **off**, so the first release detects and reports rather than deletes. `main` pushes now enter the same `group: publish-images` as `v*` tag pushes. GitHub's documented behaviour with `cancel-in-progress: false`: *"any existing `pending` job or workflow in the same concurrency group will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place."* So: tag `v1.2.0` pushed while a main-push run is in progress → the tag run goes pending → the next merge to `main` queues → **the tag run is cancelled**, and `ghcr.io/.../dataq-backend:v1.2.0` never exists. Nothing fails loudly; you get a cancelled run in the list.

Before this PR that collision was impossible, because main pushes never entered the group. The window is wide because these are uncached multi-arch QEMU builds (see nit 10). Suggested fix: `group: publish-images-${{ github.ref_type }}` (keeps main-pushes serialized with each other and tag-pushes with each other, so `:latest` still has a single writer per class), or gate the tag leg into its own job/workflow-level group.

### 3. `AzureKeyVaultStore.close()` has no test at all — delete it and the suite stays green
`backend/app/core/secrets.py:243-253`

`reset_secret_store_cache` reaches it via `getattr`, so removing the method entirely produces no AttributeError and no failing test. Every new test covers the OpenBao store; the **production** store (ADR 0024 — prod runs `azure_key_vault`) is the untested half of the fix. This is exactly the "would it still pass if the fix were reverted" criterion, and for this store the answer is yes. A `monkeypatch`ed fake `SecretClient` recording `close()` (the file already fakes the SDK elsewhere, e.g. `test_akv_store_set_reaches_sdk_through_lazy_branch`) plus an idempotency assertion would close it.

### 4. `publish-images` and `deploy.yml` now both write `:${github.sha}`, with different contents — real defect
`.github/workflows/publish-images.yml:127` vs `.github/workflows/deploy.yml:37,92,247`

publish-images pushes `dataq-{backend,frontend}:${GITHUB_SHA}` **multi-arch**; deploy.yml pushes `dataq-{backend,frontend}:${{ github.sha }}` **amd64-only** (plain `docker build`, no buildx). The two workflows are in *different* concurrency groups (`publish-images` vs `deploy-production`), so they can also run simultaneously. Before this PR, publish-images only wrote a SHA tag on tag pushes/dispatch; now every merge writes it, and every subsequent deploy of that commit overwrites it.

Consequence: the tag the header comment calls the "immutable commit SHA" is last-writer-wins and changes its architecture set. A dev on Apple Silicon pulling `:<sha>` to reproduce prod gets a working image before the deploy and `no matching manifest for linux/arm64` after. Suggested fix: on branch pushes emit `main-${GITHUB_SHA}` (or drop the SHA tag entirely for the `main` trigger) so `<sha>` stays solely owned by deploy.yml — which is what the workflow header already claims about tag ownership.

### 5. `AzureKeyVaultStore.close()` doesn't release the credential's sockets — real defect, undercuts the fix's own goal
`backend/app/core/secrets.py:243-253`, credential built at `:192`

`SecretClient.close()` is `self._client.close()` — it closes the KV client's pipeline transport only. `DefaultAzureCredential` is constructed inline at line 192, never retained, and owns a **separate** transport session per chained credential (`ChainedTokenCredential.close`: *"Close the transport session of each credential in the chain"*). So `close()` releases half the pool and leaves the token-acquisition sessions open — the same leak class #1058 is about. Fix: keep the credential on the instance and close it in `close()` (after the client). Secondary effect worth a comment: after `close()`, the next use rebuilds `DefaultAzureCredential`, re-running the whole discovery/token chain — fine for a test reset, expensive if the hot-reload caller the docstring anticipates ever lands.

### 6. `close()` on an injected-client store detaches it and silently upgrades the store to real network I/O
`backend/app/core/secrets.py:317-334`; test at `backend/tests/core/test_secrets.py:783-792`

The ownership model is right in intent, but the implementation clears `self._client` and sets `self._owns_client = True` **unconditionally**, including for a client it does not own. A store built with a `MockTransport` client therefore stops using the mock after `close()` and, on the next call, builds a real `httpx.Client(base_url=self._addr)` — i.e. it does exactly what the docstring says it must not do ("would break a caller that reuses it"), just with a different symptom: real sockets to `OPENBAO_ADDR` instead of a closed-client error. Combined with the `reset_secret_store_cache` path (which is called from the autouse conftest fixture), a test that injects a client into the singleton store and touches it after a reset would silently hit the network.

The new test asserts only `not injected.is_closed`; it never asserts `store._client is injected`, so the detach is unpinned and would not be noticed. Fix: return early when not owned (leave `self._client` and `_owns_client` untouched), and add the association assertion to the test.

### 7. `paths` filter misses two files that participate in the same skew it's fixing — real defect (same class as #1057)
`.github/workflows/publish-images.yml:56-65`

- **`.env.app.example`** — `docs/getting-started.md:76` sends evaluators to fetch it **from `main`**, exactly like the compose file. It is the second half of the eval contract: a merge that adds/renames a setting there, against a `:latest` whose `Settings` has `extra="forbid"` and closed `Literal`s, reproduces the #1056 failure mode verbatim (pydantic error naming neither cause nor fix).
- **`pyproject.toml`** — `backend/Dockerfile:53` does `COPY pyproject.toml ./`, so it is image content, yet a change to it does not republish.

Both are one-line additions to the list.

def test_get_secret_store_caches_singleton(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    """The identity assertion alone passes for ANY cached object, so also pin the
    type (#1058).

    The `cache_clear()` is what makes the setenv mean anything, and it is required,
    not defensive. `get_settings()` is `lru_cache`d; the autouse `_reset_caches`
    clears it, but the autouse `stub_run_dispatch` then imports `run_dispatch` →
    `create_celery_app()` → `get_settings()`, repopulating it from the AMBIENT
    environment. That import happens once per process, so in a whole-file run the
    cache is empty here by luck of ordering and the setenv wins; run this test alone
    against a developer `.env.app` (which ships `SECRET_STORE=openbao`) and it loses.

    Without the clear, this test asserts what the developer's env file says rather
    than what the test says — green in CI, red alone, which is precisely the
    single-test loop the local-verification rule depends on.
    """
    monkeypatch.setenv("SECRET_STORE", "env")
    get_settings.cache_clear()
    first = get_secret_store()
    second = get_secret_store()
    assert first is second
    assert isinstance(first, EnvSecretStore)

def test_openbao_close_leaves_an_injected_client_attached_and_open() -> None:
    """An injected client belongs to its caller, so `close()` must be a full no-op.

    Both halves matter. Closing it would break a caller reusing the pool. But merely
    DETACHING it is worse: the store would then build a real
    `httpx.Client(base_url=addr)` on next use, so a MockTransport-backed store would
    silently start opening live sockets to the vault after any reset — and the reset
    runs from an autouse fixture. Asserting only `not is_closed` would miss that, so
    the association is pinned too."""
    injected = httpx.Client(transport=httpx.MockTransport(lambda _r: httpx.Response(200)))
    store = OpenBaoSecretStore("http://openbao:8200", "tok", client=injected)
    store.close()
    assert not injected.is_closed
    assert store._client is injected
    assert store._client_lazy() is injected  # still the mock, not a fresh real pool
    injected.close()


def test_openbao_close_is_idempotent_and_reusable() -> None:
    store = OpenBaoSecretStore("http://openbao:8200", "tok")
    store._client_lazy()
    store.close()
    store.close()  # must not raise on an already-closed store
    rebuilt = store._client_lazy()  # rebuilt for continued use
    assert not rebuilt.is_closed
    rebuilt.close()


def test_akv_close_releases_both_the_client_and_the_credential(
    stub_azure_sdk: type[_StubSecretClient],
) -> None:
    """The PRODUCTION store (ADR 0024 runs `azure_key_vault`) must close BOTH.

    They hold separate transport sessions: `SecretClient.close()` frees only its own
    pipeline, while `DefaultAzureCredential` opens one per credential in its chain.
    Closing just the client leaves the token-acquisition sockets open — the same leak
    #1058 is about, half-fixed.
    """
    store = AzureKeyVaultStore("https://example.vault.azure.net/")

    assert client is not None and client.closed
    assert credential is not None and credential.closed
    assert store._client is None and store._credential is None

    store.close()
    store.close()  # no second close, no AttributeError on the cleared handles

fixup: address code-review findings on #1057 + #1058

All seven real defects fixed; three nits taken too.

CRITICAL — the new isinstance assertion made the singleton test pass or
fail according to the developer's .env.app rather than the test. The
monkeypatch is inert (get_settings is lru_cached) and the autouse
stub_run_dispatch repopulates that cache from the AMBIENT environment on
its once-per-process import, so the test only won by luck of ordering in a
whole-file run. Green in CI (no .env.app), red run alone — breaking exactly
the single-test loop the local-verification rule depends on. Now clears the
cache so the setenv decides; verified hermetic under SECRET_STORE=openbao
and =azure_key_vault.

Workflow:
- concurrency keyed by ref_type. One global group let an ordinary merge
  cancel a QUEUED vX.Y.Z release publish, silently leaving that version
  tag nonexistent — a collision that was impossible before this trigger.
- branch pushes tag `main-<sha>`, not a bare `<sha>`: deploy.yml already
  owns `<sha>` and builds amd64-only, so sharing the name made it
  last-writer-wins with a changing architecture set.
- paths gained .env.app.example (docs send evaluators to fetch it from
  main too — same skew, second file) and pyproject.toml (image content).
- gha layer cache, now that this build is paid per merge with the backend
  arm64 leg still under QEMU.

Store:
- close() on a NOT-owned client is now a full no-op. Detaching looked
  harmless but was worse than closing: the store would build a real client
  on next use, so a MockTransport-backed store would start opening live
  sockets after any reset — and the reset runs from an autouse fixture.
- AzureKeyVaultStore.close() now releases the credential too. It holds a
  separate transport session per chained credential, so closing only the
  client freed half the sockets — the same leak, half-fixed. This is the
  PRODUCTION store and it had no test at all; deleting the method left the
  suite green.
- reset is fail-soft, mirroring SecretStore.delete: it runs on every test
  setup and teardown, so one transport hiccup would have cascaded.
- narrowed the thread-safety claim to rebuilds; in-flight requests are not
  covered, which matters for the hot-reload caller the docstring names.

Mutation-checked: skipping the credential close, and restoring the
detaching close, each fail exactly one intended test.
